purpose: Teach: 見本/北側/理不尽/歩ん/裏切ら/尽くす/宅配/治る

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の見本写真、北側の棚にあるよ。
lines.en: The sample photos from when we were young—they're on the north-side shelf.
lines.style: Quiet, patient. Eyes moving toward memory. A small gesture of the hand, steady. No rush. The tone of someone pointing out something he's held onto for decades.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。理不尽な仕打ち、互いに乗り越えたわね。
lines.en: Yes. We got through so much unfair treatment together, didn't we.
lines.style: Soft agreement with a smile underneath. A nod that says *we know*. Gentle but solid—no doubt in the 'we'. Trailing warmth on the final word.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 長い人生、二人で歩んできた。
lines.style: Slow, deliberate. Each phrase a small stone being placed. Eyes perhaps elsewhere, into the distance. Not melancholy, but the weight of years in the voice. A kind of tenderness in the simplicity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 親戚に裏切られた時もあったけど、あなたが支えてくれた。
lines.en: There were times family let us down, but you were there when I needed you most.
lines.style: Soft but certain. A hand reaching back across time. Gratitude layered underneath—not showy, just stated plainly because it matters. Voice wavers fractionally on 'there,' then steadies.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 家族のために、お前は尽くすほうだったね。
lines.en: You're the one who always put family first, weren't you.
lines.style: Quiet observation that holds admiration. Not a question, though shaped like one. A man noticing something he's watched for decades. Respectful, slightly awed at how much she gave.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昨日、宅配でお寿司、頼んだの。
lines.style: Shift to brightness—lighter, almost conversational. A small lightness after the weight. Like moving a window to let sun back in. Matter-of-fact but with a hint of pleasure.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 風邪、治るまで、ゆっくり食べよう。
lines.en: Until your cold gets better, take your time eating.
lines.style: Gentle care in the phrasing. A quiet firmness—not suggestion, a tender insistence. The warmth of someone making sure you're looked after. Close, steady, almost a benediction.
